chapter: Sidney Bechet and the Paris festival
title: Bechet's 'Who's that boy?' story with Red Richards
summary: On the way to Toronto Bechet repeatedly failed to recognize Red Richards.

It was nice to be with Bechet because he taught me all about traditional jazz and now, and "Shimmy-Shewabble," ...them tunes. what to do with the "Muskrat Ramble" /"My Maryland," I liked the way he did "My Maryland." I've got some stories about Bechet, every time I think about it I start laughing. We were contracted to go to Toronto, Canada, to the Colonial Tavern and I had never worked with Red Richards and Sidney had never worked with Red Richards, but somehow we contacted Red Richards to come and play with us up in Toronto. So here we are at the airport, LaGuardia Field. I'm sitting with Bechet in one section of the waiting room and a little ways from there sat Red Richards and his wife, they were talking together and I didn't know Red Richards and he didn't know Red Richards and Sidney came in, he had been drinking practically all night, his hair is all mussed up and he had eye cake in his eye and he looked at me and he looked at the fellow over there, and he would say, "Who's that boy?" I said, "I don't know who he

is." Now mind you, I didn't know Red Richards and he didn't know Red Richards but we were talking about Red. That was Red Richards over there, but we didn't know it. And he says, "I know that boy. That's that boy that lives in Chicago. He's a drummer." I said, "You mean Red Saunders?" "Yeah, that's that boy, that's Red There he is over there." Saunders. / I said, "No, I know Red Saunders, I know what he looks like. That's not Red Saunders." And Bechet said again, "Who's that boy?" Finally we saw this boy get up and Red Richards came to us and he said, "My name is Red Richards, I'm going with you to Toronto." "I know that boy," said Bechet, "I know that He still didn't know Red Richards. boy." (Laughter) / But Red is such a great musician. That engagement was great.
That was when you were on your way to Paris, 1949?
No, we were on our way to Canada.
Oh, I'm sorry, Canada, yes, I'm thinking ahead. It was soon after that --
Every time we meet, Red Richards and I, Red Richards always comments, "Who is that boy?"
It was in '49 that you and Bechet went to the International Jazz Festival in Paris. It was May, wasn't it?
